image_description: A medium shot of two people on a boat holding a large fish. A woman in the foreground holds a fishing rod and supports the fish's body, while a man in orange waders behind her holds the fish by a lip gripper. The background shows a body of water and a distant bridge under an overcast sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays the characteristic elongated snout and the mouth is positioned on the underside (ventral), consistent with sturgeon anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Four distinct fleshy barbels are clearly visible hanging down from the snout area in front of the mouth.
The snout tapers to a distinct point, matching the diagnostic criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish has a long, torpedo-shaped (fusiform) body that appears large relative to the humans holding it.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, bony plates (scutes) are visible running longitudinally along the side and back of the fish, replacing typical fish scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is dark gray/brown, transitioning to a significantly lighter, whitish belly, matching the expected coloration.
The tail fin is clearly asymmetrical, with the upper lobe extending further than the lower lobe, which is the defining heterocercal trait of sturgeons.

alignment_reasoning: The image perfectly matches the target class 'sturgeon'. All diagnostic checkpoints regarding head morphology (snout, barbels, ventral mouth), body structure (scutes, fusiform shape), coloration, and tail anatomy (heterocercal) are clearly present and accurate. There are no deviations from the taxonomy knowledge.
